title: token thaw oscillation notebook
content:
Purpose:
- Quick scratchpad for an odd warmup phenomenon: after a long idle (~30m+), small-batch inference shows a repeating latency oscillation during the first ~60s of traffic (periodic bumps at ~8–12s). Trying to capture runs, hypothesis, and quick graphs for discussion.

High-level hypothesis:
- Not purely cold-start (model already loaded). Suspect interplay of token-level KV cache thawing + GPUDriver power-scaling / kernel re-priming. Could also be client-side pacing artifacts.

Environment / baseline:
- Model: open-llm-7b-quant (int8-ish profile)
- Fleet: single p4d.24xlarge equivalent host (multi-GPU), serving runtime v0.54-alpha
- Serving mode: continuous-batching enabled, dynamic KV cache retained per-tenant
- Client: synthetic harness (go), Poisson arrival with mean qps set per run
- Input profile: avg prompt length 45 tokens, generation target 60 tokens
- Batch timeout: 6ms
- Autoscale: off (single instance)

Test matrix (short):
1) Idle 0m (steady traffic) — control
2) Idle 30m — then qps spike 10 rps (small-batch), 120s capture
3) Idle 30m — then qps spike 50 rps (medium), 120s capture
4) Idle 90m — 10 rps capture
5) Idle 30m — 10 rps with client keepalive disabled

Observations (selected runs):
- Run 2 (30m idle, 10 rps): periodic p95 spikes ~8–11s intervals, amplitude from baseline 60ms -> 240ms. p50 stable ~48ms. p99 rare (~520ms) aligned with spikes. Throughput constant.
- Run 3 (30m idle, 50 rps): spikes lower amplitude (60ms -> 140ms), but higher occurrence density earlier (first 30s).
- Run 4 (90m idle): spikes slightly larger amplitude and longer tail; first spike at ~6s, then stutters ~9s.
- Run 5 (keepalive=false): spikes less regular, more noise but still present.

Quick ascii timeline (Run 2, 120s window, samples every 1s):
[0s] warm: p50 50ms p95 65ms
[6s] spike: p95 240ms
[14s] small bump: p95 180ms
[22s] near-normal
[32s] spike: p95 200ms
... repeats roughly every 8–12s for ~40s then dampens

What I instrumented for next run (todo):
- Enable nvtx / CUPTI sampling on one host to correlate kernel launches with latency bumps
- Collect GPU frequency/power logs (nvidia-smi --query) at 1s granularity
- Record runtime batching decisions (when batches flush, aggregate sizes)
- Increase batch timeout to 12ms to see if batching smoothing reduces spikes
- Run with KV cache disabled to isolate cache thaw effect

Intermediate quick hypotheses mapping:
- If nvtx shows kernel hotpath spikes concurrent with p95 spikes => driver/kernel re-priming or kernel jitter
- If GPU frequency scales down during idle and ramps up on traffic aligned with spikes => power-scaling ramp cause
- If batch flushes align (small bursts causing many tiny kernels) => batching/coalescing artifact
- If disabling KV cache removes oscillation => cache refill/first-access penalty (memory copies or small kernel invocation per layer)

Immediate experimental result (one short test):
- Increased batch timeout to 12ms, run after 30m idle at 10 rps: p95 spikes reduced amplitude (~80ms -> 120ms) and frequency reduced (spikes only in first 18s). Suggests batching smoothing helps but does not eliminate.

Notes / random observations:
- Client-side pacing jitter test: adding deliberate jitter +/-10% to inter-arrival times slightly de-synchronized spikes across runs (makes oscillation less periodic). May indicate client micro-synchrony amplifies visible periodicity.
- Some earlier runs (older runtime v0.50) showed similar phenomenon but with longer period (~15–18s). Kernel changes between v0.50 -> v0.54: moved to a new attention kernel that uses a different warm threadpool priming strategy — worth checking changelog.

Quick action items (for next 48h):
- Run 3 more instrumented experiments: nvtx + nvidia-smi + runtime trace (12–30s). Ibrahim to help on driver trace config.
- Triage: if GPU freq transitions correlate, file infra ticket to add power-state pinning option for benchmarks (temp workaround).
- If nvtx shows small kernels repeatedly invoked during spikes, open PR to coalesce layer-first-access kernels behind a single aggregated work item.
- Add a long-idle 6-hour run to see decay function of amplitude vs idle time.

Questions for sync with Mira/Ib:
- Do we want to treat this as a SLO risk? Currently only affects cold->warm short windows; customers with low-burst QPS might see recurring p95 bumps.
- Are there known scheduler/driver power policies on the CI fleet that differ from prod that could skew results?

Misc scratch:
- Possible temporary mitigation: client-side staggered warmup (send 2 warm short requests at t=0 with small jitter) reduces amplitude in ad-hoc test.
- Could be combined mitigation: runtime can inject synthetic warmup micro-batches for tenants idle > X to avoid live spikes. Tradeoff cost vs latency guarantee.

References / quick links: INF-4421 (linked) contains earlier long-idle regression notes; PR 1789 adds a threadpool change that might be related.

Conclusion (rough):
- Not a simple cold-start; multiple interacting causes. Batching smoothing helps. Next runs with kernel/driver traces should reveal whether kernel priming or power-state ramping is dominant. Prioritize traces + GPU freq logs.

End of notebook.

-- Denise
